prompt: Hey can you go through this churn prediction pipeline I wrote and tell me if anything looks off? I'm getting like 96% test accuracy which honestly seems too good, want to make sure I'm not doing anything dumb before I ship this. File is churn_pipeline.py.
assertions: Report identifies that the imputer and/or scaler are fit on the full dataframe before the train/test split (preprocessing leakage)
Report identifies days_since_cancellation_flag_set (or the engagement_score derived from it) as a target leakage feature, tied to the fact it's only populated right before churn
Report identifies that the hyperparameter search selects the best model by scoring directly on the test set rather than via cross-validation on train data
Report flags that only accuracy is reported on an imbalanced (~5%) target, and recommends an imbalance-aware metric (precision/recall/F1/PR-AUC) and/or a baseline comparison
Report flags the ~4000-category zip_code column being one-hot encoded as a cardinality problem
Report ties these findings back to explaining why the 96% accuracy is suspicious, not just listing issues in isolation
Report gives concrete, specific recommendations for each flagged issue rather than vague advice
